armF.prompt:
Below is a finished English news feature article (already translated from Japanese, no section headings). Write ONE short, natural sentence that captures the core of the story, in a way a listener can understand by hearing it just once.

Requirements:
- Exactly one sentence.
- Understandable on a single listen.
- Do not pack in multiple separate points; focus on the single most important point or twist of the story.
- Do not add any new fact, conclusion, or lesson that is not already stated in the article below.
- Keep who did what to whom, and what exactly it applied to, the same as in the Japanese source article and the Ledger below.

As a rough guide only (Trial-only guidance, not a strict rule): aim for one main clause with at most one subordinate clause, roughly 12-18 words.

Output only the sentence itself, nothing else (no quotation marks, no label like "In one line:", no Markdown heading markup).

[Article]
# Muse’s Phone Test: Human Cast Members Step In for AI

Asking AI to call a store for you feels like a glimpse of a convenient future. But in Meta’s Muse test, AI was not always the one making the calls. In some cases, trained contract workers called as human concierges and completed the conversations with the other party.

Muse is an AI agent that can call to make a haircut appointment or check whether a product is in stock. But AI was not the only one to take the stage in these calls. In effect, human cast members came on behind an AI that had received a script.

What was needed here was an explanation of the roles. Was the person answering the call being clearly told who was speaking? Meta executives admitted that it was a “mistake” to start testing calls made by contract workers without proper disclosure. A call is not a two-person play between the person who asked for it and the service. There is also the person on the receiving end.

Also, user information may be needed to complete a call. Meta employees worried that sensitive information might be shared with contract workers by mistake. This was not a story about a major information leak. Still, would information given to AI also be passed on to human staff? That can be hard to see if you are only sitting in the audience.

Meta temporarily rolled back the human concierge feature. It did not stop Muse as a whole. It plans to keep improving the phone feature and make it available only when it is ready and proper disclosure is possible.

The question raised by having AI make calls was not just whether it could get the job done. It was also about who would speak and what information would be used. If the task is handed to a human, the other person should be told that too. It seems that a convenient phone performance needs a plan that includes all of this.

[Japanese source article]
Museの電話テスト、AIの代役は人間キャスト

AIにお店への電話を頼む。便利な未来を感じる場面ですが、MetaのMuseのテストでは、電話の主役がAIとは限りませんでした。電話の一部では、訓練を受けた契約スタッフが人間コンシェルジュとして電話をかけ、相手とのやり取りを完了させていたのです。

Museは、散髪の予約や商品の在庫確認などを電話で頼めるAIエージェントです。ところが、電話の舞台に立ったのはAIだけではなかった。いわば、台本を受け取ったAIの後ろから、人間キャストが登場する仕組みです。

ここで必要なのは、配役の説明です。電話を受ける人に、話し手が誰なのかをきちんと伝えているか。Metaの幹部は、適切な開示をしないまま契約スタッフが電話をかけるテストを始めたのは「ミス」だったと認めました。電話は、頼んだ人とサービスだけの二人芝居ではありません。受け手もいるのです。

さらに、電話を成立させるには、ユーザーの情報が必要になることがあります。Metaの従業員は、機微な情報が契約スタッフに意図せず共有される可能性を心配しました。大規模な情報漏えいが起きたという話ではありません。それでも、AIに渡した情報が人間の担当者にも伝わるのか。そこは、観客席から見ているだけでは分かりにくいポイントです。

Metaは人間コンシェルジュ機能をいったんロールバックしました。Muse全体を止めたわけではありません。電話機能は改善を続け、準備が整い、適切な開示ができる場合にだけ公開する方針です。

電話の代行で問われたのは、用件を済ませられるかだけではありませんでした。誰が話すのか、どんな情報を使うのか。人間にバトンを渡すなら、そのことも相手に伝える。便利な電話劇には、そこまで含めた段取りが必要なようです。

armR.final_summary: Meta temporarily rolled back Muse’s human-concierge feature after contractors made some calls without proper disclosure.
armR.final_text:
# Muse’s Phone Test: Human Cast Members Step In for AI

Asking AI to call a store for you feels like a glimpse of a convenient future. But in Meta’s Muse test, AI was not always the one making the calls. In some cases, trained contract workers called as human concierges and completed the conversations with the other party.

Muse is an AI agent that can call to make a haircut appointment or check whether a product is in stock. But AI was not the only one to take the stage in these calls. In effect, human cast members came on behind an AI that had received a script.

What was needed here was an explanation of the roles. Was the person answering the call being clearly told who was speaking? Meta executives admitted that it was a “mistake” to start testing calls made by contract workers without proper disclosure. A call is not a two-person play between the person who asked for it and the service. There is also the person on the receiving end.

Also, user information may be needed to complete a call. Meta employees worried that sensitive information might be shared with contract workers by mistake. This was not a story about a major information leak. Still, would information given to AI also be passed on to human staff? That can be hard to see if you are only sitting in the audience.

Meta temporarily rolled back the human concierge feature. It did not stop Muse as a whole. It plans to keep improving the phone feature and make it available only when it is ready and proper disclosure is possible.

The question raised by having AI make calls was not just whether it could get the job done. It was also about who would speak and what information would be used. If the task is handed to a human, the other person should be told that too. It seems that a convenient phone performance needs a plan that includes all of this.

## In one line
Meta temporarily rolled back Muse’s human-concierge feature after contractors made some calls without proper disclosure.
